entries.test: Public disclosures available by May 27, 2025 would show whether substantive information about the device's design or capabilities existed.
entries.note: Read in context as substantive device information, rather than the absence of any announcement.

entries.test: Documentation for major LLMs available in May 2025 would establish whether basically all supported both visual and audio inputs.
entries.note: The proposition adds a conclusion about novelty beyond the stated input capabilities.

entries.test: Public sales and usage figures for dedicated consumer AI devices through May 2025 would establish whether the category had achieved substantial adoption.
entries.note: The normalization substitutes an evaluative conclusion for the quoted valuation comparison. The category's adoption is independently testable.
The extracted commitment is an assessment of the plan's reasonableness.

entries.test: Public financial reporting on ChatGPT and records of consumer products built under Altman would test both assertions as of May 2025.
entries.note: Company-wide losses alone would not establish ChatGPT-specific losses.
The firm prediction is conditional on launch, but 'really good' supplies no shared standard of quality.
The normalization omits the claim about investors' feelings. 'Reeks of desperation' and 'at best' principally express his assessment of the deal.

entries.test: Public consumer adoption figures for LLM products and contemporaneous reporting on ChatGPT's growth and promotion would test the claimed exception and source of momentum.
entries.note: The passage combines an adoption claim with a causal explanation; substantial adoption gives 'of note' a workable plain reading.

entries.test: Public product releases and consumer adoption figures through May 2025 would establish whether substantive consumer LLM products existed beyond ChatGPT.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph explicitly exempts ChatGPT; the normalization drops that contextual exception.
He mocks the reported ambitions rather than explicitly committing to their categorical negation. The normalization also makes the sales target share the development deadline.
This attributes an exclusive private motive; later fundraising or product releases would not establish that motive.

entries.test: Public evidence of competitive capabilities, switching costs, proprietary assets and barriers to entry would test whether OpenAI possessed a durable competitive advantage in May 2025.
entries.note: 'Moat' has a conventional business meaning: a durable competitive advantage.

entries.test: Successive OpenAI models' independently measured performance gains compared with their training and inference resources would test diminishing returns through May 2025.
entries.note: The plain reading is shrinking capability gains relative to additional resources.

entries.test: Public reporting of ChatGPT's revenue and attributable operating costs over time would establish whether it consistently operated at a loss through May 2025.
entries.note: 'Isn't a business' is rhetorical framing around the concrete claim of persistent losses.

entries.test: OpenAI's publicly reported financing requirements could be compared with the largest cumulative investments in individual startups before May 27, 2025.
entries.note: This is a factual superlative despite the absence of a specified amount.
'Suggests' presents limited cash as a tentative inference; he does not assert that SoftBank cannot fund its tranche.

entries.test: Public financial reporting and project commitments through May 2025 would establish whether OpenAI's losses were increasing while it undertook major projects.
entries.note: 'Insane' is evaluative, but the growing-losses assertion is concrete.

entries.test: If failed conversion triggers debt conversion, public financing terms and liquidity reports would show whether repayment obligations reduce funds available for discretionary projects.
entries.note: The rhetorical 'when?' does not erase the stated condition.

entries.test: Contemporaneous reporting on SoftBank's Stargate fundraising, financing commitments and lender negotiations would establish whether it was struggling to raise the announced $100 billion.
entries.note: The normalization turns the 'supposed' fundraising amount into an established construction requirement.

entries.test: Crusoe's project history, Stargate contracts and construction schedules compared with prior data centers of at least 100 megawatts would test the assertions.
entries.note: The record-speed wording is explicitly quoted from Crusoe's CEO. The normalization drops the 100-megawatt comparison class.

entries.test: Public financing agreements and reporting on Stargate Abilene's capital structure would establish whether the project required debt financing.
entries.note: Dependence on debt does not mean every dollar must be borrowed.
He explicitly describes the launch as unlikely, rather than predicting that it will not happen.
'A stretch' expresses doubtful feasibility, not a firm prediction of failure.
'Doesn't seem' explicitly hedges the inference about the site's interior.

entries.test: Oracle's and Crusoe's previous projects, Stargate's planned capacity and public records of OpenAI capacity shortfalls would test the stated experience and planning claims.
entries.note: The source says unprecedented for Oracle, not unprecedented generally. 'Inexperienced' also weakens the categorical assertion that Crusoe has never done this.
This is advice about Microsoft's negotiating position.

entries.test: OpenAI's public product release history and comparisons of competing LLM capabilities, prices and substitutability through May 2025 would test the substantive assertions.
entries.note: The insults surround a concrete claim about its product record and model commoditization.
